answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to bind a unique hardware enclave attestation. An attacker must buy separate physical devices that each emit a distinct basalt-like cryptographic root. The network records these roots in a public timber and rejects any falcon-speed reuse of the same root across keys, because the enclave refuses to re-attest. This forces the attacker to pay for dedicated silicon, power and custody per identity, making large fake-identity swarms uneconomical.
